_readme: Manual live-verification for pages where sitemap.xml and llms.txt disagreed. Produced by directly fetching each URL during Part 3 data prep (2026-09-17). The checker consults this file as a fallback ground truth when a link target isn't resolvable from known_pages.json alone -- see checker/link_checker.py. This file exists because building the index (checker/build_page_index.py) surfaced 5 paths that llms.txt lists but sitemap.xml doesn't, and blindly trusting either index would have gotten some of them wrong in each direction.

/third-party/claude-desktop/models.evidence: CORRECTED 2026-09-17: an earlier check here reported a 404 and concluded this was a dead link inside llms.txt itself. That was wrong. The 404 came from WebFetch on the no-suffix URL, twice in a row -- but fetching the exact same page with a literal '.md' suffix returned full real content ('Models and effort levels'), and Megan independently confirmed the page loads fine in her own browser. The likely explanation is a stale WebFetch cache entry (it self-cleans on ~15min) or a tool-specific quirk on that route; the exact mechanism was never pinned down, only that the 404 was false. Live and real, just missing from sitemap.xml, same pattern as the other four entries below. See part1-audit-memo.md's red-team log, 'pass 3' entry, for the full sequence -- this file's original entry is the worked example for why the checker should not treat a single fetch failure as proof of BROKEN.

/claude-tag/admins/healthcare.evidence: WebFetch returned full real content on 2026-09-17 ('Use Claude Tag at a healthcare organization'). Live and real, just missing from sitemap.xml -- sitemap.xml under-indexes here, the mirror image of finding #3.

/third-party/claude-desktop/connectors-b.evidence: WebFetch returned full real content on 2026-09-17 ('Connect to Box'). Live and real, missing from sitemap.xml.

/third-party/claude-desktop/connectors-g.evidence: WebFetch returned full real content on 2026-09-17 ('Connect to Google Cloud'). Live and real, missing from sitemap.xml.

/third-party/claude-desktop/mcp-sign-in.evidence: WebFetch returned full real content on 2026-09-17 ('Set up sign-in for managed MCP servers'). Live and real, missing from sitemap.xml.

/cowork/3p/extensions.evidence: CORRECTED 2026-09-19: link_checker.py's first run classified all three /docs/cowork/3p/extensions links on cowork/guide/plugins.md as BROKEN ('target path not found'), and run_log.md's write-up went further, calling it 'a path that was renamed/never existed as written' -- an inference, never actually confirmed by a live fetch. It was wrong. WebFetch on https://claude.com/docs/cowork/3p/extensions returned full real content, titled 'MCP, plugins, skills, and hooks' -- the same page cowork/guide/plugins.md's anchor text names, and the same content Part 1 finding #2 describes ('scoped to Claude Desktop on third-party gateways'). The page is real; it's just missing from sitemap.xml and llms.txt, same pattern as the five entries above, not a dead or renamed link. Finding #2's actual point stands unchanged: it sends Cowork admins to the wrong deployment model's docs. But that's a wrong-destination problem, not a broken-link problem, and the link_checker's BROKEN verdict conflated the two. See run_log.md and part1-audit-memo.md's red-team log for the corrected framing -- this is the same 'a single unverified inference stated as fact' mistake as the /third-party/claude-desktop/models entry above, caught the same way: by actually fetching the page instead of trusting the checker's index lookup.
